subject: English
passage: Marine biologist Mala Dhar and colleagues studied the naturally occurring algal communities found on both the shells and feeding appendages of wild sea turtles in coastal waters. The researchers discovered many of the same algal species on both the turtles' shells and feeding appendages. To explain this, the researchers pointed to the turtles' frequent contact with the seafloor during feeding and noted that sediment stirred up from the bottom could bring bottom-dwelling algae into contact with the shells. Alternatively, the researchers noted that ocean currents, which may be a source of algae in the water column, could also deposit algae onto the seafloor. Either explanation suggests that ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: algae transported by ocean currents are typically less nutritious to sea turtles than bottom-dwelling algae are.
choices.B: many algae on sea turtle feeding appendages may have been deposited by means other than sediment stirring.
choices.C: some algae on sea turtle shells and feeding appendages may share a common source.
choices.D: sea turtle shells and feeding appendages are particularly susceptible to harmful algal overgrowth.

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because it presents the conclusion that most logically follows from the text's discussion of algal distribution on sea turtles. The text explains that researchers found the same algal species on both shells and feeding appendages and proposed two explanations. The text points out that either bottom algae could reach shells through sediment stirring, or water column algae could reach the seafloor through ocean currents. Because both explanations involve algae moving between the same two environments, it's reasonable to infer that algae found in different locations on the turtles may originate from shared environmental sources.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect because this conflicts with the text. One of the proposed explanations is specifically that algae on feeding appendages were deposited through sediment stirring during bottom feeding.
